skill.name: treasures
skill.description: Guides agents through Treasures Finance APIs for tokenized stock discovery, portfolio reads, trade quotes, transaction submission, and cross-chain USDC bridging. It covers public and delegated wallets on Ethereum and Solana.
skill.summary: Guide Treasures Finance API workflows across tokenized stocks, USDC, wallets, Ethereum, and Solana.
skill.author: starchild-ai-agent

security_audit.summary: All 54 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, expected API examples, defensive proxy guidance, and an HTTP error code. However, the skill explicitly teaches agents to route geo-fenced securities requests through VPN exits. A prose warning cannot enforce eligibility, so these bypass instructions create material legal and financial abuse risk.

remediation.issue: The skill teaches agents to bypass geographic controls on securities trading endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the VPN bypass instructions. Require server-enforced identity, residency, KYC, and jurisdiction checks before any quote or trade.

remediation.issue: Wallet signing and trade submission lack a mandatory user approval checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Show wallet, chain, asset, amount, fees, slippage, and destination. Require fresh, explicit confirmation before signing or submitting.

remediation.issue: Installation examples invoke an unpinned external skills package.
remediation.suggestion: Reference an immutable commit or trusted release, and require user confirmation before running any npx installation command.

content.user_title: Manage Tokenized Stock and USDC Operations
content.value_statement: Tokenized asset workflows combine multiple APIs, wallets, chains, signatures, and jurisdiction rules. This skill organizes Treasures Finance discovery, portfolio, quote, trade, bridge, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes the public B2B API from the delegated-wallet API.
Explains tokenized stock discovery, portfolio reads, and trade history.
Documents buy and sell quote requests for Ethereum and Solana wallets.
Describes wallet ownership proofs and delegated signing models.
Covers USDC bridge quotes and multi-leg transaction sequences.
Maps common HTTP responses to routing, schema, signature, and holdings issues.
limitations: Referenced subskills are not included in this package, so their safeguards cannot be verified here.
A 451 response is an access restriction, and this skill must not bypass eligibility controls.
Examples do not verify prices, fees, KYC status, token allowlists, or legal eligibility.
Financial actions can be irreversible and require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Review a Wallet Portfolio
use_cases.description: Summarize tokenized stock positions and trade history without preparing a transaction.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Eligible Trade
use_cases.description: Collect a quote, validate the wallet and chain, then present details for approval before execution.

use_cases.title: Diagnose API Failures
use_cases.description: Separate routing, request schema, signature, and insufficient holdings errors during integration testing.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Stocks
prompt_templates.prompt: List the tokenized stocks available through Treasures Finance. Show ticker, provider, supported chain, and quote currency. Use read-only endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Treasures portfolio for wallet [address] on [chain]. Summarize positions and recent trades. Do not sign or submit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Trade Quote
prompt_templates.prompt: For an eligible user in [jurisdiction], prepare a [buy or sell] quote for [ticker] and [amount]. Present all costs and await approval.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-Chain Operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a USDC bridge from [source chain] to [destination chain], followed by a [ticker] trade. Identify every approval, signature, fee, and failure checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Summarize the portfolio for an Ethereum wallet without making changes.
output: Tokenized equity positions: GOOGL and NVDA

output_examples.input: Prepare a quote to sell 0.01 GOOGL with one percent maximum slippage.
output_examples.output: Quote preparation is ready. Confirm wallet, jurisdiction eligibility, expected proceeds, fees, and slippage before any signature or submission.

output_examples.input: Explain why the quote returned HTTP 451.
output_examples.output: The request reached a geographic access control before authentication. Do not treat this as a signature error or bypass an eligibility restriction.

best_practices: Verify jurisdiction, KYC status, and token eligibility before requesting a trade quote.
Require explicit user approval immediately before every wallet signature and transaction submission.
Confirm wallet, chain, ticker, amount, fees, slippage, and destination at each step.
anti_patterns: Do not use a VPN to bypass a geographic or securities eligibility restriction.
Do not set a global HTTP_PROXY value for all agent traffic.
Do not select a wallet API without confirming where the user assets are held.

faq.question: Can this skill execute trades?
faq.answer: It documents quote and execution workflows. Actual execution needs the referenced APIs, wallet access, and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which networks are covered?
faq.answer: The instructions cover Ethereum and Solana for tokenized equities and USDC operations.

faq.question: Which wallet route should I use?
faq.answer: Use the public B2B route for user-owned wallets. Use the delegated route only when the user explicitly selects a Treasures wallet.

faq.question: What does an HTTP 451 response mean?
faq.answer: It indicates a geographic access restriction before authentication. Confirm eligibility and do not bypass the restriction.

faq.question: Does the skill require credentials?
faq.answer: Public workflows require wallet signatures. Delegated workflows may require a Treasures API key.

faq.question: Does this skill provide financial or legal advice?
faq.answer: No. Users must independently verify asset terms, pricing, tax treatment, and jurisdiction eligibility.
